title: SmartBundle: Unified Multi-Mode Hosted Endpoint PRD + Launch Checklist
creator: Elena Park
description: PRD for SmartBundle: a single hosted API endpoint that accepts a multi-mode request (chat/completion/embeddings/rerank) and dynamically routes to optimized model variants and execution paths. Goal is to reduce integration surface for customers while preserving per-mode behavioral contracts and operational controls (SLOs, cost accounting, rollout policies).
goals: Provide a single canonical endpoint (POST /v1/smartbundle) that supports chat, completion, embedding, and rerank workloads with a mode field and adaptive routing.
Maintain mode-specific behavioral contracts (determinism bands, embeddings vector shape, rerank scoring semantics) equivalent to dedicated endpoints.
Reduce customer integration effort by 30% relative to maintaining four separate endpoints in our onboarding survey baseline.
Preserve per-request observability and per-token billing parity with existing hosted endpoints.
Support streaming responses for chat/completion and synchronous embeddings/rerank with consistent error surface.
Provide canary rollout and graded degradation policies so tenant traffic can fail over to dedicated mode variants without outages.
non_goals: This PRD does not cover on-prem/private deployment packaging for SmartBundle (Private variant to follow in a separate project).
No changes to existing per-tenant billing models beyond tagging requests with mode and model (billing integration ticket will map tags to existing rate tables).
Not building a universal tokenizer—clients must continue to use model-specific tokenization guidance for cost estimates.
requirements: API contract: request schema must include 'mode' with allowed values [chat, completion, embedding, rerank], 'model', and 'input' with mode-dependent shape. Optional 'profile' field for cost/latency hints.
Behavioral compatibility: chat must support message arrays, system/user/assistant roles, function calling and streaming chunked output identical to hosted-chat endpoint semantics.
Completions: support prompt + temperature/top_p controls, regeneration endpoint semantics, and deterministic sampling when seed provided.
Embeddings: return vector with model-dictated dimensionality, base64 or JSON array depending on client Accept header; include embed_cost_estimate in response metadata.
Rerank: accept list of candidates + query, return stable score ordering and per-candidate explainability token (optional) consistent with hosted-rerank semantics.

Routing: runtime must select model variant optimized for the mode and tenant based on policy (latency-first for chat, cost-first for embeddings, accuracy-first for rerank) with explicit override in request.
Observability: token-level cost, model variant used, routing decision, latency breakdown (queue, compute, marshal), and KV-cache hit/miss should be emitted to telemetry for each request.
Fallbacks: when primary model variant unavailable, route to pre-configured fallback variant with clear degradations in response metadata.
SLA/SLO: per-tenant 99th percentile request latency targets must be configurable by lane; default SLOs: chat p95 < 400ms (short prompts), embedding p95 < 1200ms, rerank p95 < 1500ms.
Security: requests must honor tenant KMS keys for any ephemeral caching of prompt context and include audit log entries for model selection and fallback events.
Schema validation: server must return 400 for malformed mode-specific inputs and a consistent error schema for clients.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests: end-to-end tests covering each mode pass in CI with >= 95% success across representative synthetic traffic profiles.

Behavioral conformance: curated eval suites for chat/completion/embedding/rerank show no regression >1% against current hosted endpoints on quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity/rerank-ndcg as appropriate).
Latency & cost: staging workloads show cost per 1k tokens within 10% of dedicated endpoints and meet p95 latency SLOs for each mode under target traffic shape.
Telemetry: request-level telemetry includes model_variant, routing_reason, kv_cache_hit boolean, and token_cost tags; dashboards show these metrics for at least 72 hours in staging.

Backward compatibility: an adapter page for existing hosted endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) is published with migration examples and SDK snippets, and existing clients continue to operate unchanged for 90 days after launch if they do not opt into SmartBundle.
Security review: threat model and KMS audit completed, no high severity open findings.
Runbook & rollback: operational runbook exists with two-step rollback (disable adaptive routing, then redirect to per-mode endpoints) and a tested rollback drill executed in staging.
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal): enable SmartBundle for Redwood dev org only; monitor eval metrics and telemetry for 7 days.
Beta (selected customers): open to 5 early adopter accounts with an opt-in flag; limit traffic to 5% of their calls and run nightly quality/regression checks.
Gradual ramp: increase exposure by 10% per week with automatic quality gates; pause ramp if eval regressions exceed thresholds or error rate spikes > 3x baseline.

General availability: full public launch after 4-week successful ramp and completion of marketing/SDK docs; announce deprecation plan for any redundant adapter endpoints once adoption > 50% for new integrations.
Fallback policy: if primary model fails, runtime will emit 429/503 only if no fallback available; otherwise respond with fallback variant and metadata describing differences.
dependencies: ENG-67112 (routing policy engine) must implement tenant-level policy overrides and expose routing_reason header.
ENG-68400 (telemetry enrichment) to add model_variant and kv_cache_hit fields to payloads.
ENG-69001 (streaming gateway) to support chunked streaming semantics for SmartBundle chat/completion mode.
PM-449001 (billing mapping) to map mode tags to existing billing tables and ensure invoicing parity.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Behavioral regressions when collapsing separate endpoint codepaths into shared pipeline. Mitigation: keep mode-specific codec layers and run exhaustive mode-specific evals in CI.
Risk: Increased complexity in routing leading to harder incident triage. Mitigation: routing_reason header, enriched traces, and a dedicated routing-dashboard with per-tenant heatmaps.

Risk: Cost differences surprising customers due to cross-mode caching. Mitigation: include embed_cost_estimate and cost_estimate hints in API; provide an opt-out to disable cross-mode caching per tenant.
Risk: Security surface growth for function-calls in consolidated endpoint. Mitigation: require explicit function policy whitelist per tenant and KMS-scoped caching.
metrics: Adoption: % of new integrations using SmartBundle within 60 days of SDK launch.
Quality: mode-specific eval pass rates (target >= 99% non-regression on critical tests).
Performance: p95 latency per mode vs baseline; target deltas: chat <= +50ms, embedding <= +150ms, rerank <= +200ms.
Cost: average token cost / 1k tokens and embedding cost per vector; track delta to previous endpoints.
Reliability: error rate and fallback rate by tenant; target < 0.5% fallback for top-tier tenants.
